summary: Introduces Nuggets — standalone, independently-learnable concepts reusable across sections/essays without duplicating content, flashcards, or review state — as a new layer between essay sections and flashcards, restructures essays around a compact main spine, and wires explicit [[nugget:key]] Markdown references, navigation, and a matching ChatGPT round-trip through reading, authoring, flashcard generation, exploration, and oral-examination freshness.

classification.why_application: Nuggets are essaycards-specific domain content — a new layer in this app's own learning-content hierarchy (essay -> section -> nugget -> flashcard), with app-specific validation (nugget-key convention, [[nugget:key]] reference resolution, derived section_nuggets resync), app-specific navigation semantics (reading-position preservation, source navigation from a review session), and app-specific ChatGPT round-trip shapes. None of this is reusable technical capability — it only has meaning within EssayCards' own content model.
non_goals: Knowledge-graph UI or automatic semantic link discovery
Automatic conversion of every historical essay to use nuggets
Automatic reassignment of historical flashcards to nuggets by guessed semantic match — assignment is explicit only, one card at a time, via POST /flashcards/upsert
A nugget-scoped GET /flashcards/due or GET /flashcards/stats endpoint — reviewing a nugget-linked card for real spaced repetition still goes through the existing essay/section-scoped focus session
An app-level guard against the flashcards.nugget_id ownership/cascade risk described in this sprint's schema comment and risks below — documented only, by explicit decision
Nugget-key rename support — nugget_key is upsert-by-key only, with no in-place rename path, same as slug/anchor_slug/card_key
Markdown-CLI front-matter authoring of essays.main_spine_markdown — JSON/API-ingest-only this sprint (see contracts.invariants)
A new bulk/atomic flashcard-generation-from-nugget import endpoint — the frontend issues one POST /flashcards/upsert call per generated card, reusing the existing single-card endpoint (see risks)

Deciding or wiring up where nugget examination-freshness is surfaced in the UI or API — this sprint adds only the storage/echo mechanism and a pure comparison helper; the draft explicitly leaves the surfacing location open
classification.not_platform: Nugget content, the [[nugget:key]] reference syntax, the resync-on-ingest behavior, and the ChatGPT round-trip prompts are all meaningful only within EssayCards' own content model and its existing ingestion/export conventions. Nothing here is exposed as a reusable capability for other Atlas applications; if another app later needs a similar reusable-content-unit concept, that is the point to consider a platform extraction — not now.

invariants: nugget_key is globally unique (essaycards.nuggets.nugget_key), author-assigned, validated against SLUG_LIKE_RE (^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$, promoted this sprint from essays.py's private _SLUG_LIKE_RE into backend/ingest.py as the one canonical definition — R-CON-BP-07); no code path auto-slugifies or auto-lowercases it.

Nugget create/update is always upsert-by-nugget_key (`on conflict (nugget_key) do update set title = ..., body_markdown = ..., updated_at = now()`); nugget_key is never a SET column, so a title/body edit can never change the key. There is no nugget-key rename path this sprint.

essaycards.section_nuggets is derived, never author-maintained: on every section upsert (markdown CLI or JSON API, via the single shared backend.ingest.upsert_document), the section's [[nugget:key]] references are extracted and the association rows are fully resynced — missing ones inserted, stale ones deleted. This is the one explicit exception to the app's general no-delete-on-re-ingest policy; it only ever removes a section_nuggets row, never a nuggets row or a flashcards row.

extract_nugget_keys(markdown_text) (backend/ingest.py, new) strips fenced code blocks and inline code spans with a regex pass FIRST, then matches \[\[nugget:([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)\]\] on what remains — the extraction regex's key character class now matches SLUG_LIKE_RE exactly ([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+), so any valid nugget_key (mixed case included) is always referenceable from a [[nugget:key]] reference in any section/main-spine Markdown. Resolution against a captured key remains exact-match/case-sensitive (no case-folding) — only the set of characters the regex will capture changed, not the comparison semantics. Corrects the character-class mismatch originally specified in 00_draft.md §1/§2, per 11_design_review.md Confirmed Problem 1 / Minimal Change Set item 1.

backend.ingest.upsert_document's FIRST step (before _upsert_essay is called) collects the union of extract_nugget_keys() over doc.get('main_spine_markdown', '') and every section's body_markdown, resolves them against essaycards.nuggets in one query, and raises IngestionError naming EVERY unresolved key at once (not just the first) if any is missing. Nothing is written before this check runs, so the existing `except Exception: conn.rollback(); raise` wrapper is a harmless no-op rollback on this new failure path too. An unresolved nugget reference is ALWAYS a validation error — no placeholder nugget is ever auto-created.

This nugget-reference validation is identical on both ingestion paths (markdown CLI and POST /essays/ingest) because it lives inside the single shared upsert_document core — unlike the pre-existing card/section-collision check, which remains exactly as asymmetric as it is today (JSON pre-checks via _check_card_section_collisions, markdown CLI does not). Only the new nugget-reference check is unified; nothing about the existing asymmetry changes.

backend/routers/essays.py::ingest_essay wraps its upsert_document(conn, doc) call in try/except IngestionError as exc: return api_error('VALIDATION_ERROR', str(exc)) — IngestionError can now be raised by upsert_document itself (the new nugget-resolution step), not only by markdown parsing, so the JSON-path router must catch it. backend/ingest.py's CLI _main() already wraps both _parse_document and upsert_document in one try/except IngestionError block — no change needed there.

essays.main_spine_markdown is settable via POST /essays/ingest only (optional top-level key, default '' on omission, same optional-key/on-conflict-do-update convention as category/sort_index/status). backend/ingest.py::_parse_front_matter (markdown-CLI grammar) is UNCHANGED this sprint — an essay ingested via the markdown CLI always upserts main_spine_markdown = '' via upsert_document's doc.get('main_spine_markdown', '') default. This is the resolution of the 'main-spine authoring on the CLI path' open question named in 00_draft.md's closing Note.

POST /flashcards/upsert's card.nugget_id follows R-CON-AL-04/05 exactly: key OMITTED from the card object -> existing assignment untouched (both on update and, vacuously, on create, where there is nothing to touch); key present as JSON null -> assignment cleared; key present with a non-empty string value -> resolved against essaycards.nuggets.id and set, or VALIDATION_ERROR if it does not resolve to an existing row. The SQL implements this with a single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE whose nugget_id SET expression is `case when <touch_nugget_id> then <resolved_value_or_null> else essaycards.flashcards.nugget_id end` — never a second UPDATE statement and never an omitted-vs-present ambiguity collapsed to the same SQL path.

flashcards.essay_id and flashcards.section_id remain required and unchanged this sprint — a nugget-linked card is still anchored to exactly one owning essay/section, even though the nugget itself may be referenced from other sections/essays. This is the documented ownership/cascade limitation (see risks) — no app-level guard is added.

QuestionOverviewView's existing per-question edit form (inline q/a/level fields, POST /flashcards/upsert) gains a nugget assignment control: a <select> populated once per view mount from GET /nuggets plus a 'No nugget' entry, initialized from the question row's now-present nugget_id (GET /essays/{essay_id}/questions). Save ALWAYS sends card.nugget_id explicitly — the selected nugget's id, or JSON null for 'No nugget' — never omitted, mirroring the existing 'level is required on every call, never defaulted' precedent already established for this same form. This completes the R-CON-AL-05 round trip for nugget_id: UI representation of the cleared state = the selectable 'No nugget' option; frontend payload = explicit id or null, never omission; backend interpretation and persisted state were already correct per R-CON-AL-04 and are unchanged. The one-way 'Generate flashcards from a nugget' creation flow (internal_flow step 13) is unaffected — it continues to always set nugget_id to a value at creation time. Closes 11_design_review.md Hard Rule Violation 2 / Minimal Change Set item 3.

GET /nuggets/{id}/flashcards is a flat, read-only display list (id, card_key, question, answer, level, essay_id, section_id) with NO scheduling fields (no next_due_at, no is_new/is_recent/scheduled_interval_seconds) and is deliberately NOT due-queue-shaped — reviewing a nugget-linked card for real spaced repetition still goes through the existing essay/section-scoped focus session the card already belongs to, identical to a legacy card. GET /flashcards/due and GET /flashcards/stats gain no nugget-scoping parameter this sprint.

Flashcard source navigation (ReviewSessionView): current.nugget_id set -> 'Flashcard -> Nugget' control, opening an in-page overlay (NOT a route navigation) with a further link to GET /nuggets/{id}/sections ('referenced by'); current.nugget_id null -> unchanged legacy 'Jump to passage' route navigation to ReaderView#anchor_slug. Opening/closing source material from an active review session must never unmount ReviewSessionView or interrupt/reset the session.

Reading-position preservation (ReaderView): a [[nugget:key]] reference renders as an in-app NuggetLink, never a real <a> tag. Clicking it opens an in-page overlay/panel (component state within ReaderView — an activeNuggetId/nuggetPanelStack, not react-router navigation), so ReaderView never unmounts and the reader's scroll position is preserved with no full page reload when the panel is closed. A nugget's own body_markdown may itself reference further nuggets; the panel supports this recursively via a client-side id stack (push on click-through, pop on back), never leaving the overlay.

remarkNuggetRefs(titleMap) (new remark plugin, src/ShellEntry.tsx) visits only mdast 'text' nodes (unist-util-visit) — by the time remark hands off, fenced code blocks and inline code spans are already separate code/inlineCode node types, so a [[nugget:...]] written inside either is structurally invisible to a text-node visitor; no hand-written fence/span detection is needed on the frontend (unlike the backend's regex-based extract_nugget_keys, which must do this itself because it operates on raw text, not a parsed AST). Each match in a text node becomes an mdast link node: resolved key -> url 'nugget:<key>', child text = titleMap[key]; unresolved key -> url 'nugget-missing:<key>', child text = the raw key. `components={{ a: NuggetLink }}` branches on the href scheme: nugget: -> in-app overlay open (see above); nugget-missing: -> non-clickable, styled as broken, key text never silently rendered as if valid; anything else -> ordinary <a>, unchanged behavior for normal links/images.

titleMap for a section's rendering is built client-side from that section's own `nuggets: [{nugget_key, title}]` field on the already-fetched essay-detail response — computed once per section render, never fetched per link. The essay's main_spine_markdown builds its titleMap as the client-side union of every section's nuggets field AND the essay's own main_spine_nuggets: [{nugget_key, title}] field (new this correction round — resolved server-side at read time via extract_nugget_keys(main_spine_markdown) against essaycards.nuggets, independent of section co-reference; see internal_flow's main_spine_nuggets_resolution step) — so a nugget referenced only in main_spine_markdown, never in any section, still resolves to a title instead of rendering as nugget-missing. Closes the R-CON-AL-03 gap identified in 11_design_review.md Hard Rule Violation 1 / Minimal Change Set item 2.

Section spine revision package drop-detection (IngestView): when ReaderView's 'Export section' action succeeds, the focus section's focus_section_nuggets key set is stashed in sessionStorage keyed by section_id. When IngestView parses a pasted payload whose shape includes focus_section_id, it looks up that stashed key set, extracts the returned section's CURRENT nugget keys via a new client helper extractNuggetKeysClient (a TS mirror of backend/ingest.py::extract_nugget_keys — same strip-fences-then-match-[[nugget:key]] approach), and computes the set difference (previously required minus currently present). A non-empty difference renders a non-blocking warning banner naming the dropped key(s) — SUBMISSION IS NEVER BLOCKED by this check, only a warning is shown, per 00_draft.md §8 ('surfaces, not silently blocks'). The sessionStorage entry is read once and cleared on read.

backend/exploration.py::build_exploration_package: when the flashcard's nugget_id is set, `context` is `{'nugget_body_markdown': <live nugget body>, 'nugget_key': ..., 'nugget_title': ...}` INSTEAD OF `{'section_body_markdown': ...}` — a replacement, not an addition, per 00_draft.md §8 ('becomes ... instead of'). When nugget_id is null, `context` is unchanged: `{'section_body_markdown': ...}`. This is a discriminated-union response shape on a bespoke, Dataset-exempt, EssayCards-owned JSON contract; the frontend ExplorationPackage TS type and EXPLORE_PROMPT_INTRO/buildExploreClipboardText must branch on which key is present.

backend/examinations.py::build_export_package adds a per-section `nugget_versions: {nugget_key: <live nuggets.updated_at ISO8601>}` object (current references only) alongside the existing `section_version` field. validate_import_body accepts an OPTIONAL per-result `nugget_versions` key (a JSON object mapping nugget_key -> ISO-8601 timestamp string, or absent/null); import_results stores it VERBATIM into the new section_examinations.nugget_versions_at column — never recomputed at import time, same echo-through-import handling as section_version_at. Absent/null on import -> stored null ('predates this feature' semantics is preserved even for a fresh import that simply omits the key, e.g. a hand-crafted or legacy-shaped result).

A pure helper backend/examinations.py::nugget_freshness_flags(recorded: dict | None, current: dict) -> list[str] implements the §9 comparison rule (recorded is None -> [] / skip; else any key in current missing from recorded, or present with a different value, is flagged) but is NOT wired into any endpoint or UI this sprint — the draft explicitly leaves 'wherever ultimately surfaced' open. Its inputs and output are fully realizable from data already stored (R-CON-BP-11/R-CON-AL-03); only its call site is deferred.

All new/changed GET endpoints returning UI-visible tabular data return Dataset per R-CON-BP-04: GET /nuggets, GET /nuggets/{id}, GET /nuggets/{id}/flashcards, GET /nuggets/{id}/sections. GET /nuggets/authoring-package and GET /nuggets/{id}/generate-flashcards-package are bespoke-JSON Dataset exemptions on the same rationale class already documented for GET /essays/{id}/examination-package and GET /flashcards/{id}/exploration-package (self-contained interchange artifacts copied to the clipboard for an external LLM, not rendered by a Dataset-consuming UI component).
failure_modes: VALIDATION_ERROR — POST /essays/ingest or the markdown CLI referencing an unresolved [[nugget:key]] (one message naming every missing key at once) — 400 ApiError (JSON path) / IngestionError, no DB write (both paths)
VALIDATION_ERROR — POST /nuggets/upsert with a missing/blank nugget_key or title, or a nugget_key not matching SLUG_LIKE_RE — 400 ApiError, no write
VALIDATION_ERROR — POST /flashcards/upsert with card.nugget_id present (non-null) but not resolving to an existing essaycards.nuggets row, or not a well-formed id — 400 ApiError, no write
NOT_FOUND — GET /nuggets/{id}, GET /nuggets/{id}/flashcards, GET /nuggets/{id}/sections, GET /nuggets/{id}/generate-flashcards-package with an unknown nugget id — 404 ApiError

NOT_FOUND — GET /nuggets/authoring-package / GET /nuggets/{id}/generate-flashcards-package with an unknown essay_id, a section_id not belonging to that essay, or (authoring-package only) an unknown nugget_id when one is supplied — 404 ApiError

Broken/unresolved nugget reference in ALREADY-STORED Markdown (a nugget referenced at ingest time later has no row — cannot occur through the app itself since resolution is enforced at ingest and nuggets are never deleted by the app, but is possible via direct SQL): remarkNuggetRefs renders it as a non-clickable 'nugget-missing:<key>' link, never silently as if valid. This is a rendering-time fallback, not a new ingest-time failure mode.

Partial-application risk (documented, not solved) — 'Flashcard generation from a nugget' import issues one POST /flashcards/upsert call per AI-generated card (no new bulk/atomic endpoint, reusing the existing single-card endpoint per 00_draft.md §8 and the non-goals list); if call N of M fails, cards 1..N-1 are already saved while N..M are not. See risks.

Ownership/cascade gap (documented, not guarded) — deleting the essay/section that owns a nugget-linked flashcard removes the card even if another essay still references the same nugget. No delete endpoint exists anywhere in the app today, so this has no live trigger; see risks.

consumes: Starlette Request.json() — used by POST /nuggets/upsert (new) on the same raw-body/no-Pydantic precedent as POST /essays/ingest, POST /flashcards/upsert, POST /flashcards/{id}/review, POST /examinations/import, POST /flashcards/exploration/import
unist-util-visit@5.1.0 — new explicit direct frontend dependency, used only by remarkNuggetRefs
provides: HTTP API mounted at /api/essaycards (FastAPI, uvicorn) — unchanged mount, methods (GET, POST), and CORS policy

internal_flow.name: extract_nugget_keys
internal_flow.description: backend/ingest.py::extract_nugget_keys(markdown_text) strips fenced code blocks (```...```) and inline code spans (`...`) with a regex pass, then matches \[\[nugget:([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)\]\] on the remainder, returning the set of referenced keys. Pure, no DB access. Character class corrected to match SLUG_LIKE_RE per 11_design_review.md Minimal Change Set item 1.
outputs: set[str] of referenced nugget keys

internal_flow.name: nugget_reference_resolution
internal_flow.description: upsert_document's new first step (before _upsert_essay): compute the union of extract_nugget_keys() over doc.get('main_spine_markdown', '') and every section's body_markdown; one query `select id, nugget_key from essaycards.nuggets where nugget_key = any(%s)`; any key in the union not present in the result set is collected and, if non-empty, raised as a single IngestionError naming every missing key. Nothing is written before this point.
inputs: doc: dict (as parsed/validated by either ingestion path)
cur: an open cursor within upsert_document's transaction
outputs: nugget_id_by_key: dict[str, str] (only reached if no key is missing) | raises IngestionError

internal_flow.name: essay_upsert_with_main_spine
internal_flow.description: _upsert_essay (extended) now also writes main_spine_markdown (doc.get('main_spine_markdown', '')) in both the INSERT and the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET list.
inputs: title, slug, category, sort_index, status, main_spine_markdown
outputs: essay_id, was_inserted

internal_flow.name: section_nuggets_resync
internal_flow.description: Per section, once _upsert_section returns section_id: compute that section's own extract_nugget_keys(body_markdown), map to nugget ids via the nugget_id_by_key built in step 2, then `insert into section_nuggets (section_id, nugget_id) select %s, unnest(%s::uuid[]) on conflict do nothing` followed by `delete from section_nuggets where section_id = %s and not (nugget_id = any(%s::uuid[]))` (the empty-array case correctly deletes every existing association when a section no longer references any nugget). Only ever removes section_nuggets rows, never nuggets or flashcards rows.
inputs: section's referenced nugget ids (subset of nugget_id_by_key)
outputs: section_nuggets rows resynced to exactly the section's current references

internal_flow.name: ingest_essay_error_translation
internal_flow.description: backend/routers/essays.py::ingest_essay now wraps its upsert_document(conn, doc) call in try/except IngestionError as exc: return api_error('VALIDATION_ERROR', str(exc)) — the new failure path from step 2 must surface as a 400 ApiError on the JSON path, exactly like every other _validate_ingest_body failure.
inputs: doc (already structurally validated by _validate_ingest_body, now including main_spine_markdown)
outputs: typed ingest-summary record (200) | ApiError VALIDATION_ERROR (400, either from pre-write structural validation or from the new nugget-resolution step)

internal_flow.name: nugget_upsert
internal_flow.description: POST /nuggets/upsert validates {nugget_key, title, body_markdown?} then `insert into essaycards.nuggets (nugget_key, title, body_markdown) values (...) on conflict (nugget_key) do update set title = excluded.title, body_markdown = excluded.body_markdown, updated_at = now() returning id, created_at, (xmax = 0) as was_inserted`.
outputs: {id, nugget_key, title, created: bool} (200) | ApiError VALIDATION_ERROR (400)

internal_flow.name: flashcard_upsert_nugget_tristate
internal_flow.description: backend/routers/flashcards.py::_validate_upsert_body reads card_raw.get('nugget_id', _UNSET) to distinguish omitted from present. If present and non-null, must be a non-empty, well-formed-uuid string. _upsert_question then, if the key was present, resolves it against essaycards.nuggets (VALIDATION_ERROR if it does not exist) and issues a single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE whose nugget_id SET clause is `case when %s then %s else essaycards.flashcards.nugget_id end` (touch flag, resolved-value-or-null) — so an omitted key never disturbs an existing assignment and an explicit null always clears it.
outputs: flashcards.nugget_id set/cleared/untouched per R-CON-AL-04 | ApiError VALIDATION_ERROR if a supplied id does not resolve

internal_flow.name: nuggets_by_section_lookup
internal_flow.description: A new private helper (backend/routers/essays.py::_nuggets_by_section(cur, section_ids) -> dict[str, list[dict]]) joins section_nuggets to nuggets for a set of section ids, ordered by nugget title asc, and is reused by get_essay, export_essay, export_section, and list_essay_questions to attach each section's {nugget_key, title} pairs without duplicating the join SQL four times.
outputs: dict[section_id, list[{nugget_key, title}]]

internal_flow.name: section_export_nugget_context
internal_flow.description: export_section additionally selects the essay's main_spine_markdown and, scoped to focus_section_id only, the FULL {nugget_key, title, body_markdown} for every currently-referenced nugget (`join section_nuggets ... where section_id = %s`) as focus_section_nuggets — richer than the generic light {nugget_key, title} pairs step 8 attaches to every section in the array.
outputs: package gains main_spine_markdown (top-level) and focus_section_nuggets (top-level, focus section only)

internal_flow.name: section_export_drop_detection_client
internal_flow.description: Frontend-only: ReaderView.handleExportSection stashes sessionStorage['essaycards:sectionExport:'+sectionId] = JSON.stringify(pkg.focus_section_nuggets.map(n => n.nugget_key)) right before copying the clipboard text. IngestView, on parsing a pasted payload that has a focus_section_id field, reads and clears that sessionStorage entry, extracts the returned focus section's CURRENT nugget keys via extractNuggetKeysClient (TS mirror of extract_nugget_keys), and renders a non-blocking warning banner naming any previously-required key no longer present. Never blocks submission.
inputs: pasted JSON payload (client-side, parsed but not yet submitted)
sessionStorage entry stashed at export time
outputs: optional warning banner text; no effect on whether Submit is enabled

internal_flow.name: nugget_authoring_package
internal_flow.description: GET /nuggets/authoring-package resolves essay_id/section_id (404 if either fails, or section does not belong to essay), optionally resolves nugget_id (404 if given but unresolvable), reads the essay's title/main_spine_markdown, the section's anchor_slug/heading/body_markdown, and — if nugget_id was given — the nugget's own row plus extract_nugget_keys() resolved over its body_markdown as connected_nuggets ({nugget_key, title} pairs); nugget is null and connected_nuggets is [] when nugget_id was omitted (drafting a brand-new nugget). Read-only.
outputs: bespoke JSON package (200) | ApiError NOT_FOUND (404)

internal_flow.name: generate_flashcards_package
internal_flow.description: GET /nuggets/{id}/generate-flashcards-package resolves the nugget (404 if missing) and the essay_id/section_id context (404 if either fails), reads the nugget's {nugget_key, title, body_markdown}, and the nugget's current flashcards via the same query as GET /nuggets/{id}/flashcards (adding question/answer for AI context) as existing_flashcards. Read-only.
inputs: essay_id, section_id (query, context anchor for cards to be created)
outputs: bespoke JSON package (200) | ApiError NOT_FOUND (404)

internal_flow.name: generate_flashcards_import_client
internal_flow.description: Frontend-only: the AI reply is parsed client-side as {cards: [{level, q, a}, ...]}; for each entry the frontend issues one POST /flashcards/upsert with {essay_slug: pkg.context.essay_slug, section_id: pkg.context.section_id, card: {level, q, a, nugget_id: <the nugget id already known from the route/component state>}}, sequentially, collecting per-card success/failure. No new backend endpoint — reuses POST /flashcards/upsert once per card (see risks: not atomic across the batch).
outputs: N sequential POST /flashcards/upsert results, each with nugget_id pre-set to the source nugget

internal_flow.name: exploration_context_by_nugget
internal_flow.description: backend/exploration.py::build_exploration_package, after reading the flashcard row (now including nugget_id), branches: if nugget_id is set, join essaycards.nuggets and set context = {nugget_body_markdown, nugget_key, nugget_title} (no section_body_markdown key present); else context = {section_body_markdown} exactly as before.
outputs: export package (200) whose context shape depends on nugget_id | None if flashcard_id invalid/not found (mapped to 404 by the router, unchanged)

internal_flow.name: examination_export_nugget_versions
internal_flow.description: backend/examinations.py::build_export_package additionally selects, per section, the currently-referenced nuggets' {nugget_key: updated_at} via section_nuggets/nuggets, attached as nugget_versions on each section dict alongside the existing section_version.
outputs: package sections gain nugget_versions: {nugget_key: ISO8601}

internal_flow.name: examination_import_nugget_versions_echo
internal_flow.description: validate_import_body accepts an optional per-result nugget_versions (dict[str,str] of nugget_key -> ISO-8601 timestamp, or absent/null); import_results stores it verbatim as section_examinations.nugget_versions_at (jsonb) in the same INSERT as the existing columns. Never recomputed; absent/null stored as SQL null.

internal_flow.name: nugget_freshness_helper
internal_flow.description: backend/examinations.py::nugget_freshness_flags(recorded, current) -> list[str]: recorded is None -> [] (predates feature, skip); else every key in current missing from recorded, or whose recorded value differs from current[key], is included in the returned (sorted) list. Pure function, no DB access, not called by any endpoint or UI this sprint.
inputs: recorded: dict[str,str] | None (from a stored nugget_versions_at)
current: dict[str,str] (freshly computed live nugget_versions for the same section)
outputs: list[str] of stale/changed nugget_keys

internal_flow.name: reader_main_spine_and_section_rendering
internal_flow.description: ReaderView renders essay.main_spine_markdown and each section.body_markdown through <ReactMarkdown remarkPlugins={[remarkNuggetRefs(titleMap)]} components={{a: NuggetLink}}>. internal_flow.name: review_session_nugget_source_nav

risks.risk: flashcards.nugget_id ownership/cascade gap: a flashcard reachable via a shared nugget from another essay is still owned by only its own essay_id/section_id; deleting that owning section/essay would remove the card even though another essay still references it via the nugget.
risks.impact: Data loss for the OTHER essay's apparent access to that card if the owning essay/section were ever deleted. The app has no delete endpoint anywhere today (essays/sections/flashcards/images are all upsert-only), so this risk has no live trigger through the app; it is latent, not exercised. Documented in three places (schema.sql, CLAUDE.md, here) per explicit decision, with no app-level guard added — same pattern as the Sprint02 card/section-move asymmetry already tracked in this app's architecture history.

risks.risk: 'Flashcard generation from a nugget' import issues one POST /flashcards/upsert call per AI-generated card, not a single atomic bulk operation.
risks.impact: If call N of M fails (e.g. a malformed card partway through the AI's reply), cards 1..N-1 are already saved while N..M are not, leaving a partially-applied batch. No new bulk/atomic endpoint is introduced this sprint (see non_goals/forbidden) — the UI must report per-card success/failure so the user can retry only the failed cards; this is a documented limitation, not a defect.

risks.risk: src/ShellEntry.tsx grows further from its already-large single-file size (~2960 lines pre-sprint) with this sprint's substantial additions (NuggetPanel, remarkNuggetRefs, multiple new export/import views).

risks.risk: Recursive nugget-to-nugget references (a nugget's own body_markdown referencing another nugget) inside the NuggetPanel overlay have no depth limit specified.
risks.impact: A pathological authoring mistake (nugget A references B references A) could let a user push/pop the panel's id stack indefinitely without a cycle, though each push is a deliberate user click (not automatic), so this is a UX nuisance at worst, not an infinite-loop bug.
